Search cyclic-symmetric codes (9x17, 3x51, 17x9, 51x3) by optimising only orbit representatives with pulled-back exponential repulsion, then break symmetry gradually and LP-polish.
direction: Search symmetry-constrained configurations from scratch instead of perturbing the record: represent points as pairs of complex numbers $(z_1,z_2)\in S^3$ and generate 153 points as 9 orbits of size 17 under $(z_1,z_2)\mapsto(\omega^a z_1,\omega^b z_2)$, $\omega=e^{2\pi i/17}$, for several exponent pairs $(a,b)$, also trying 3 orbits of size 51 and unions involving smaller special orbits. Optimise only the orbit representatives with a log-sum-exp or exponential-repulsion objective over the full generated 153-point Gram matrix, screen many random representative initialisations cheaply, fully relax the best few, then gradually break the symmetry by adding an unconstrained perturbation whose amplitude increases from 0 to about 0.05-0.15, followed by smooth relaxation and final LP polishing. This explores highly structured basins that generic basin hopping from the asymmetric record is unlikely ever to reach.

Delete-and-reinsert continuation removing the rattler plus overloaded 7-8-contact hubs or a whole spherical cap, annealing survivors with exponential repulsion, then greedily reinserting LP-refined max-min holes one-by-one with relaxation and LP polish.
direction: Use delete-and-reinsert continuation centred on the rattler and overloaded hubs: remove the zero-contact rattler plus combinations of 7-, 8-contact and spatially clustered points, for total removals of about 8, 12, 20 and 30 points; optimise the remaining easier subconfiguration with annealed exponential repulsion (for example $\beta$ increasing from 30 to 300 over 800-1500 steps), then find insertion holes by evaluating 30,000 random unit vectors, locally optimising the best separated candidates on $S^3$ to minimise their maximum dot product with existing points, and reinsert points one at a time with a short smooth relaxation and LP polish after each insertion. Try both hub-focused removal and removal of a whole spherical cap, because the goal is to let the surviving points expand into a genuinely different configuration before the removed points are placed into newly created large holes.

idea: Coordinated cluster-drift plus worst-point void reinsertion to change the jammed contact topology, annealed soft-max repulsion for basin exploration, and short trust-region LP probes with long final LP polish.
Crossover of diverse annealed basins with Kabsch-Hungarian alignment and cap mixing
direction: Build a population of genuinely distinct local optima and recombine them: generate 6-12 from-scratch configurations with different random seeds and annealed Riesz/log-sum-exp schedules, lightly LP-polish each, and characterise each by its sorted contact-degree sequence and number of contacts so that near-duplicates of the record basin can be discarded. For pairs of distinct parents, align them by an optimal orthogonal transformation in $\mathbb R^4$ (SVD/Kabsch), match their points with Hungarian assignment, create children by taking a spherical half-space or cap of points from one parent and the complementary matched points from the other, remove duplicates, then repair the child by farthest-hole insertion, annealed smooth optimisation and LP polishing. Maintain diversity by accepting children whose contact graphs differ materially from both parents, using the remaining time for crossover/mutation cycles while always retaining the loaded record as the returned fallback if no child improves it.

idea: Variable-N continuation around 153 — strip highest-contact points down to 148–152 and rebuild (or overshoot to 154–156 and prune) with best-of-20000 hole insertion plus smooth/LP relaxation to find a new evenly-stressed basin.
direction: Use variable-$N$ continuation to escape through neighbouring cardinalities: starting from `best.npy`, repeatedly remove the highest-contact point (and, in separate branches, random high-contact points), LP-polish briefly after each removal down to $N=148$–152, then rebuild to 153 by inserting each new point at the best of at least 20,000 random sphere candidates followed by short smooth relaxation and LP polishing; also try overshooting to $N=154$–156 and pruning the point whose removal gives the lowest polished maximum. Run several removal/insertion orders with different seeds, retain every intermediate 153-point result, and reserve the final 25–30 seconds for LP-polishing the best one, always falling back to the loaded record if a branch fails.

Rattler-free surgery by deleting cluster-incident or random contacts, moving along the tangent Jacobian nullspace (floppy modes), then LP polishing.
direction: Perform contact-graph surgery by travelling along floppy modes: load `best.npy`, identify contacts with slack $<10^{-9}$ and build their tangent-space Jacobian on $S^3$, then repeatedly delete either all contacts incident to a random spatial cluster of 4-8 points or a random set of 10-20 contacts, compute the resulting 1- to 5-dimensional Jacobian nullspace by SVD, and integrate points along random nullspace combinations with renormalisation, using step sizes around 0.005-0.05 and stopping when a previously inactive pair reaches the current maximum or a deleted contact rises appreciably. Alternate several such excursions with 2-5 second LP polishes, keep the incumbent as a fallback, and spend most of the 180 seconds testing different deleted clusters/contact sets rather than repeatedly perturbing all 153 points isotropically.

idea: Enforce $C_{17}$ ($9$ reps) and $C_9$ ($17$ reps) cyclic symmetry on $\mathbf R^4=\mathbf C^2$ and optimize only representatives with Adam on annealed exponential repulsion pulled back through inverse rotations, then break symmetry with $10^{-3}$ noise and LP-polish.
direction: Retry symmetry-constrained search in a deliberately minimal, crash-safe form: identify $\mathbb R^4=\mathbb C^2$, impose a $C_{17}$ action $(z_1,z_2)\mapsto(e^{2\pi i/17}z_1,e^{2\pi ia/17}z_2)$ for $a=1,\ldots,8$, and optimise only 9 orbit representatives (generating all 153 points by expansion), using ordinary Adam on the annealed exponential-repulsion objective with gradients aggregated back through the inverse rotations—no Hungarian matching, external code, or LP inside the symmetry phase. Try each $a$ briefly, also try the analogous $C_9$ action with 17 representatives, then break symmetry with $10^{-3}$ tangential noise and LP-polish the best expanded codes; wrap the entire experiment in `try/except`, validate shape and finiteness, and return the polished record on any failure so this family is finally evaluated rather than lost to a load error.

idea: Second-shell active-set surgery forcing 1-3 near-contact pairs apart under frozen-neighbour trust-region LPs to jump basins, then relax and polish.
direction: Perform active-set surgery with second-shell pairs: compute all pair slacks, select non-contact pairs with slack between about $10^{-5}$ and $5\times10^{-4}$, and run modified trust-region LPs that keep all current contacts below $t$ while forcing one to three chosen second-shell pairs to satisfy $\langle x_i,x_j\rangle\le m-\eta$ for $\eta\in[10^{-4},10^{-3}]$ and trust radii $0.01$–$0.05$. To keep each LP fast, freeze points outside the endpoints and their contact neighbours, include movable–frozen pair constraints explicitly, test many randomly chosen pair combinations for roughly 100 seconds, then smooth-relax and fully LP-polish any feasible configuration whose true maximum is within $0.001$ of the incumbent.

idea: Freeze a rigid core and rebuild weakly-constrained clusters with greedy farthest insertion plus core-fixed annealed repulsion and short LP unfreezing to find a new evenly-stressed basin.
direction: Rebuild the weakly constrained part against a frozen core: choose clusters of 8, 12, or 16 points consisting of the rattler, points with at most four contacts, and some of their neighbours; delete the cluster, place its points greedily from 8,192 random candidates by maximising the minimum cosine against the frozen core and already-placed points, then optimise only the movable points for about 1,000 annealed-repulsion steps with the core fixed before unfreezing everything for a short LP polish. Repeat over many random clusters and acceptance temperatures until about 130 seconds have elapsed, keeping a candidate whenever it improves the incumbent or changes at least 20% of the contact edges without worsening the score by more than $2\times10^{-4}$, and finish with a long LP polish of the best 153-point configuration found.

idea: Rattler-hole reinsertion with cooperative neighbour displacement, rattler-weighted annealed repulsion and LP polishing filtered by rattler contacts.
direction: Exploit the rattler as a free insertion variable while moving its prospective neighbours cooperatively: identify the zero-contact point and all points with at most four contacts, generate at least 50,000 random sphere candidates plus local tangent-gradient minimisation of $\max_j\langle y,x_j\rangle$ to find the five largest well-separated holes, then for each hole place the rattler there and simultaneously displace its six nearest points along the tangent directions away from it by several trial distances between 0.01 and 0.08 before any global relaxation. Run annealed exponential repulsion with the rattler’s pair weights multiplied by about five so that it is forced to acquire three or four near-contacts, followed by trust-region LP polishing, and retain the result only if the rattler has contacts within $10^{-5}$ of the final maximum; use strict internal deadlines and always fall back to the incumbent if no trial finishes.

idea: Diverse pool of random and Kronecker-Hopf quasi-uniform starts with short log-sum-exp annealing and Jaccard-based basin selection plus one cap transplant.
direction: Build a genuinely diverse pool of independent basins instead of repeatedly perturbing the record: generate eight starts from random points and Hopf/Fibonacci-style quasi-uniform points on $S^3$, optimise each with a fixed short schedule in which the log-sum-exp inverse temperature increases gradually and the step size decreases, and characterise each result by its near-contact graph using pairs within $10^{-3}$ of its maximum. Discard or deprioritise basins whose graphs are nearly identical to the incumbent by Jaccard similarity, LP-polish only the best two mutually diverse basins, and if they remain worse than the record use one graph-guided transplant in which a spherical cap containing a differently arranged patch is retained while the complementary points are re-optimised against it; implement this with elementary NumPy operations, frequent time checks, and no fragile alignment or symmetry machinery.

Rattler-void reinsertion plus coordinated low-contact cluster shaking with core-fixed exponential repulsion and short trust-region LP unfreezing to jump basins.

Hub-centred contact-graph surgery deleting an overloaded 7-8 contact hub plus neighbours and greedily reinserting points into scaffold holes with subset-only annealed repulsion before global smoothing and LP polishing.
direction: Perform contact-graph surgery on overloaded local clusters rather than kicking random points: compute contacts at slack $10^{-7}$ and pair stresses from the LP dual variables if available, select a hub with seven or eight contacts together with four to six of its contacted neighbours, delete that cluster, keep the remaining points initially fixed, and reinsert the deleted points one at a time by continuous minimax hole optimisation against the scaffold followed by joint tangent-space optimisation of only the reinserted subset. After all deleted points have been reinserted with a different adjacency pattern, unfreeze the whole configuration for short exponential smoothing and LP polishing; repeat for several distinct hub-centred and low-contact-centred clusters, scoring trials first by whether their contact graph differs materially from the incumbent and only then by maximum cosine.
